summary: Reason about who must arrive at a synchronization point and why unsafe waiting can deadlock a GPU.
outcomes: Choose thread, warp, block, cluster or grid synchronization appropriately.
Diagnose divergent barriers and unsafe cross-block waiting.
sequence: Start with a shared tile whose producer is late.
Draw required arrival and visibility edges.
Compare block barriers and warp synchronization with participation masks.
Expose divergence, incomplete participation and scheduling deadlock.
Replace a global barrier with separate launches or a supported cooperative launch.

visual.question: Which participant prevents the next phase from becoming valid?
visual.interaction: Toggle participating lanes or blocks and inspect arrival counts and dependencies.

practice.task: Repair two deadlocking kernels and justify the synchronization scope.
practice.success: All required participants arrive; no assumption that all blocks are resident together remains.
